q: Non-metals are the chemical elements that mostly lack the characteristics of metals.
e: True. Non-metals are the chemical elements that mostly lack the characteristics of metals.

q: Non-metals are located on the left side of the Periodic Table.
e: False. Non-metals are located on the left side of the Periodic Table.

q: Among non-metals, 6 non-metals are solids, and 11 non-metals are gases.
e: True. Among non-metals, 6 non-metals are solids, and 11 non-metals are gases.

q: Only one non-metal, chlorine, is a liquid.
e: False. The non-metallic solid, graphite is a conductor. Only one non-metal, chlorine, is a liquid.

q: Nitrogen is the non-metallic element with the symbol N and atomic number 7.
e: True. Nitrogen is the non-metallic element with the symbol N and atomic number 7.

q: A nitrogen atom has 7 protons, 7 neutrons, and 7 electrons.
e: True. A nitrogen atom has 7 protons, 7 neutrons, and 7 electrons.

q: A nitrogen molecule has two nitrogen atoms joined together by two covalent bonds.
e: False. Hydrocarbons are compounds in which carbon and hydrogen atoms are bonded to each other by covalent bonds. An N2 molecule holds two nitrogen atoms with a triple covalent bond, which is why nitrogen is so unreactive. A nitrogen molecule has two nitrogen atoms joined together by two covalent bonds.

q: Nitrogen is a colourless gas with a pungent smell.
e: False. Ammonia is a colourless gas with a characteristic pungent smell. Nitrogen is a colourmore gas with a pungent smell.

q: Nitrogen has a very low boiling point of -196°C.
e: True. Nitrogen has a very low boiling point of -196°C. Nitrogen has a very low boiling point, which is why it is a gas at room temperature and is separated from liquid air.

q: The Earth's atmosphere is made up of 78 percentage of nitrogen.
e: True. The Earth's atmosphere is made up of 78 percentage of nitrogen. About 78 percent of clean dry air is nitrogen. The mixture of gases around Earth is the atmosphere, and that mixture exerts pressure.

q: There is a large amount of nitrogen in the Earth's crust.
e: False. Minerals are inorganic substances found in the Earth's crust. Rusting is the corrosion of iron in the presence of both air and water. There is a large amount of nitrogen in the Earth's crust.

q: Nitrogen can be found in fairly rare minerals such as Chile saltpetre ($NaNO_3$).
e: True. Nitrogen can be found in fairly rare minerals such as Chile saltpetre (NaNO_3). Saltpetre and similar nitrate minerals are uncommon natural sources of combined nitrogen.

q: Industrially, elemental nitrogen can be manufactured by fractional distillation of liquid air.
e: True. Industrially, elemental nitrogen can be manufactured by fractional distillation of liquid air. Fractional distillation of liquid air separates nitrogen, oxygen and argon by boiling point. Industrial nitrogen is taken from liquid air by fractional distillation.

q: In the preparation of nitrogen from air, caustic soda solution is used to remove oxygen.
e: False. In the preparation of nitrogen from air, caustic soda solution is used to remove oxygen.

q: Carbon dioxide free air is passed over heated copper which absorbs oxygen to form copper(II) oxide.
e: True. Carbon dioxide free air is passed over heated copper which absorbs oxygen to form copper(II) oxide.

q: Nitrogen gas is collected by the upward displacement of water.
e: False. Nitrogen dioxide is collected by the upward displacement of air.

q: If dry nitrogen is required, it may be passed through a U-tube containing glass beads wetted with concentrated sulphuric acid.
e: True. If dry nitrogen is required, it may be passed through a U-tube containing glass beads wetted with concentrated sulphuric acid. Concentrated sulphuric acid is viscous, dehydrating and oxidising as well as strongly acidic. Concentrated sulphuric acid is a strong acid, a dehydrating agent and an oxidising agent.

q: The main use of nitrogen is in the manufacture of ammonia gas.
e: True. The main use of nitrogen is in the manufacture of ammonia gas.

q: Some important nitrogen fertilisers are ammonium nitrate, ammonium sulphate, and urea.
e: True. Some important nitrogen fertilisers are ammonium nitrate, ammonium sulphate, and urea.

q: Since nitrogen has 5 electrons in its outermost shell, its oxidation numbers vary from -3 to +5.
e: True. Since nitrogen has 5 electrons in its outermost shell, its oxidation numbers vary from -3 to +5. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion. Nitrogen has five outer electrons, so its oxidation numbers run from -3 to +5.

q: The oxidation number of nitrogen in ammonia ($NH_3$) is -3.
e: True. The oxidation number of nitrogen in ammonia (NH_3) is -3. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion. Oxidation number is the charge an atom would have if electrons in each bond were assigned to the more electronegative atom.

q: The oxidation number of nitrogen in dinitrogen oxide ($N_2O$) is +2.
e: False. The oxidation number of nitrogen in nitric acid (HNO_3) is +5. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion. Oxidation number is the charge an atom would have if electrons in each bond were assigned to the more electronegative atom.

q: The oxidation number of nitrogen in nitric acid ($HNO_3$) is +5.
e: True. The oxidation number of nitrogen in nitric acid (HNO_3) is +5. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion. Oxidation number is the charge an atom would have if electrons in each bond were assigned to the more electronegative atom.
